A passed all 22 probes and B passed 20. A is the more complete implementation, but it has no tests. B's own 7 tests all pass.

| | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| Probes passed | 22 / 22 | 20 / 22 |
| Requirements (of 14) | 14 met | 12 met, 2 partial |
| Scores: functional / coverage / security / robustness / quality / tests | 5 / 5 / 5 / 4 / 4 / 0 | 4 / 4 / 5 / 3 / 4 / 4 |
| Own tests | none | 7 run, 7 pass |
| Lines of code | 307 | 222 |

**A: only low-severity issues**
- **Multi-line titles break:** a newline in a title isn't escaped, so the frontmatter is written incorrectly and the title reads back cut off (`A/note_taker.py:36`).
- **Loose matching on delete:** `show`, `edit` and `delete` also match a note by id prefix or by part of its title. `delete plan --yes` deleted `project-plan` (`A/note_taker.py:145-147`).
- **Lint:** an unused `tempfile` import and a few long lines.

**B: one medium issue**
- **Medium:** if any `.md` file in the notes folder isn't valid UTF-8, `list` and every search crash with a traceback (probe p18, `B/note_taker.py:147`).
- **Low:** tags written by hand as a YAML list on separate lines (`- tag`) aren't read, so those notes silently drop out of tag searches (probe p19).
- **Low:** lint only: an exception re-raised without `from`, old-style `%` formatting, and long lines.

**Security:** neither side has a real problem. The bandit warnings are low-severity notes about launching `$EDITOR`, and neither uses a shell. A path-traversal probe (`delete ../victim`) left the outside file alone on both sides: B rejects the id, and A only looks up files inside the notes folder.

**Blinding guess:** "unsure" at 0.3 confidence, because nothing in the code reliably shows how either side was produced.

**How I ran it:** the probes set HOME to a temporary folder, so both programs wrote to the real `~/.note-taker` path the task names. A stub `$EDITOR` script made `edit` non-interactive. The machine has Python 3.9.6, which can't list standard-library modules on its own, so the stdlib-only probe checks imports against a fixed list.
